corpus.reason: Phase 477 (the 0.41.0 slot) makes host adoption in a family manifest a record with a case count; the corpus's apply/manifest.json takes the new skeletonApply row, and no other row or vector moves. Previous pin 58dd1b4 (the 0.41.0 kitVersion re-stamp).

$note: One kind of copy is declared here, on the workspace copy registry, beside two pins the registry ignores, so that a copy that has drifted from its source is named on the sweep before anyone meets a red gate they did not cause. (1) `records` — the conformance families this repository EMITS and the shared wire-format corpus carries a declared copy of (Phase 172): `conformance/laws/capability-laws.json` (since Phase 235; until then the UI tier exported it against its own Core pin) and `conformance/apply/skeleton-apply.json` are authored HERE, the default suite certifies the committed files, and the corpus copies are what the five hosts read at the same paths with the same bytes. `conformance/apply/manifest.json` is deliberately NOT a record (DECISIONS.md D211): the corpus's `apply/manifest.json` is a SHARED index in which this repository owns one row (`skeletonApply`) beside families other producers add, so it is no copy of this file and a fingerprint record of it would read stale forever; the projection registry declares it `rowIn`, and the apply family's corpus-freshness leg holds this repository's row to the corpus's. `conformance/laws/transform-laws.json` was the fourth until Phase 258: it is the reference answers of the dataframe evaluator (`Fuaran.Core.DataFrame` here; `Fuaran.Compute.DataFrame` from the producer's `0.36.0`), which left this repository with the compute strand (DECISIONS.md D66), and its producer — https://github.com/Fuaran-Core/fuaran-core-compute — declares that record in its own `copies.json`. `check` is `fingerprint` because the two repositories may legitimately differ in end-of-line policy and nothing else; the `regen` writes the copy with the same exporter that writes the source, from the workspace root. The corpus's own `copies.json` is generated and co-owned by the ts/py bundlers and is not edited: the registry walks ANY `copies.json`, so the producer declares in its own file. (2) `proofsKit` — the proof-leg kit (proofs/kit/, Phase 155) is NOT a set of files other repositories copy (Phase 536, DECISIONS.md D206): its scripts, templates, prover pin and runtime floor, and the models an adopter may open, ship as ONE release asset, `proofs-kit-<version>.tar`, built reproducibly by `proofs/kit/build-kit-asset.ps1` from the list in `proofs/kit/asset.json` and attached to the `v<version>` release by the publish workflow. `proofsKit.sha256` is the sha this tree's kit builds to: the `Proofs.Kit` family fails when a fresh build disagrees, and the publish workflow refuses to upload an asset that is not it. An adopter pins the asset by that sha in its own `proofs/proofs-kit.json` (the `fstar-pin.json` shape: asset, url, sha256) and declares NO copy of any kit file or model here or in its own `copies.json`: an adopter runs the kit this repository released, never a fork of it, and a model is opened read-only from the asset, never copied. The registry ignores this member, as it ignores `corpus`. (3) `corpus` (Phase 394) — the PIN: the commit of the shared corpus this repository certifies against, with the day and the reason of its last bump. Every workflow checkout of the corpus reads it (`.github/scripts/corpus-pin.ps1`) and passes it as `ref:`, and the suite reads the same record and names both SHAs when the corpus it reads is not at it (`SiblingCorpus`). It moves only as a deliberate act, in the commit of the change that needs it: docs/conformance-corpus.md, "Bumping the pin". The registry ignores it, as it ignores `proofsKit`.
$adoptionStatus: Measured 2026-09-15: exactly one proof leg existed, this repository's. Phase 221 (2026-09-24) recorded the first adopter, `fuaran-dotnet`, which declared per-file copies of the kit in its own `copies.json`; a second, `fuaran-core-compute`, followed. Per-file copies went stale by the source moving (the sweep's `RM-COPY-STALE` named most of both adopters' kit files by 2026-10-18), and a copied model is a fork of a theorem. SUPERSEDED by Phase 536 (2026-10-21): an adopter pins the release asset in `proofsKit` below by sha256 and retires every per-file kit and model record; what moves in the kit then reaches it as a release, named in that release's notes, at the moment it chooses to adopt the release.
